## LLM Recipe

### 1.1 Data Curation &amp; Tokenization

#### [No Single Tokenizer Feature Reliably Predicts Downstream Language Model Performance](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21679>)

Across three small-model suites and nine languages, this study finds that popular tokenizer metrics correlate inconsistently with downstream quality, even when individual task correlations appear strong. The results support validating tokenizer choices on representative tasks and languages instead of treating compression or a single intrinsic score as a reliable accuracy proxy.

**Published:** 2026-10-15 · **First seen:** 2026-10-17T10:02:15.889Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Tokenizer Evaluation, Multilingual Models, Intrinsic Metrics

**Public availability:** 2026-10-16T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21679>) · [Code](<https://github.com/shikhar-srivastava/vista-training>) · [Project](<https://huggingface.co/collections/shikhar-srivastava/vista-130m>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Full Sections 3–10 and the model, evaluation, statistical and robustness appendices inspected again. Three suites cover 14 TokSuite 1B models, 45 usable TIMTC 350M models after nine OOV exclusions, and multilingual VISTA 130M/350M models; 29 intrinsic metrics and 48 distinct benchmark tasks span nine languages. The analysis z-scores accuracy within language and task, corrects multiple comparisons, controls parameter counts and repeats the analysis after excluding near-chance cases. The strongest aggregate correlations are only r=0.27, 0.24 and 0.22, while signs and rankings change across tasks, languages and suites. A metric explains at most an additional 0.021 R-squared beyond model size; pairs of intrinsic metrics reach at most 0.09 joint R-squared. Existing VISTA training code and model collections were verified both in the prior run and today. This was a reviewed but unpublished reserve on October 17, below that run’s selected contributions; fresh reassessment now includes its useful tokenizer-selection lesson within the remaining 72-hour lookback. Its original October 17 first-seen time is preserved. No indexing delay is claimed.

**Limitations:** These observational correlations do not show that tokenizers do not matter or that a better metric cannot exist. Models are at most 1B parameters, some tasks are near chance, language coverage and suite training budgets differ, vocabulary sizes change embedding parameter counts, and annotated intrinsic resources are uneven across languages. Compression can still reduce cost without predicting accuracy. The VISTA link is training code, not the complete current paper-analysis pipeline. The main analysis repository, unavailable with 404 responses during the prior run, loaded today, but its sole observed code commit is October 18 at 21:13Z, after the report’s 10:00Z cutoff. That later artifact is not used as an in-window contribution or advertised as available by the cutoff; its exact first public visibility is not inferred from Git metadata. An undated author homepage lists the title without a paper link and does not establish an earlier full-method release.

### 1.7 Reinforcement Learning &amp; Reasoning

#### [Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22324>)

After supervised warm-starting, this recipe trains an 8B model to generate three scientific ideas in one rollout and rewards each idea’s judged quality multiplied by its difference from earlier ideas. The resulting sets outperform quality-only RL on the authors’ document-grounded benchmark, suggesting a practical way to discourage duplicate proposals while leaving scientific validity and source grounding as separate checks.

**Published:** 2026-10-15 · **First seen:** 2026-10-18T21:41:55.857Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Set-level RL, Scientific Ideation, Quality-Diversity Rewards

**Public availability:** 2026-10-16T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22324>) · [Project](<https://github.com/ManyaWadhwa/diverge_ideation>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Full primary HTML, including the reward, training, judging, human-study and execution appendices, inspected. Sections 2–6, Equations 2 and 7, Tables 1, 3, 4 and 11, and Appendices B–F describe one K=3 rollout, a shared GRPO set advantage, a quality-times-nearest-prior-distance reward, schema gating and a capped length penalty. SFT and RL use 7,172 English NLP training instances; the main test has 1,740 instances across 16 scientific domains. In Table 1, the Qwen3-8B no-thinking model reaches judged Creative Utility 0.64 versus 0.21 after SFT and 0.38 with impact-only RL; idea distance is 0.88 versus 0.38 for impact-only RL. Grounding falls from 0.90 after no-thinking SFT to 0.61 after RL; the thinking variant trades lower utility (0.51) for higher grounding (0.81). The four-expert, 60-instance human pilot reports 2.17 promising ideas per set versus Claude’s 2.20. Appendix F’s execution pilot has 15 source instances (14 for the thinking variant), using a budgeted coding agent and its own experimental verdicts, not independently validated scientific discoveries. The author-linked repository currently contains only a coming-soon README. First inspected during this run; the paper is an unreported October 16 new-submission batch contribution inside the 72-hour lookback, so it is a delayed discovery rather than an October 18 release. Original October 15 receipt date is retained.

**Limitations:** All results are author-reported. LLM judges define quality, distance, grounding and most benchmark outcomes; a 2026 test-year split alone does not prove absence of training contamination. The within-set reward does not ensure diversity across the population: IdeaSeed method-type entropy is 0.65 for no-thinking and 0.73 for thinking, below the reported human 0.87. The DARLING comparison also changes initialization, rollout grouping and clipping, so it does not isolate only where diversity is rewarded; the impact-only ablation is the cleaner comparison. Four experts and 15 execution instances are small pilots, and the execution agent’s self-reported support/refutation is not verified discovery. Training uses an external distance-judge API in addition to the local H200 allocation. Code, data and models are promised, not released in the verified project. No broad scientific-discovery or universal SoTA claim is supported.

## AI Agent Dev

### 2.8 Agent Evaluation &amp; Security

#### [GraphACM: Graph-based Action Consistency Measurement for Uncertainty Quantification in LLM Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22031>)

GraphACM aligns repeated agent runs into a shared state-action graph and measures whether they choose the same actions in comparable decision contexts. This training-free signal localizes behavioral disagreement and distinguishes more reliably solved tasks in the tested environments, helping builders assess execution stability without treating consistency as a correctness guarantee.

#### [AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21624>)

AgentPerturb builds matched clean and noisy agent tasks by varying user requests, procedures, inherited context and tool contracts across missing, distracting and incorrect information. Its two-environment study exposes different failure patterns and costly recovery tails, providing a practical test design for robustness that clean benchmark scores can miss.

## AI Training &amp; Inference Infra

### 3.4 Attention, KV Cache &amp; Memory Systems

#### [LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22179>)

LCT stores BF16 weights, saved activations and optimizer buffers in a lossless exponent-coded format, using parallel GPU encoding, fused updates and a shared overflow arena for repeated compression during training. The new paper quantifies a memory-versus-step-time trade-off and explains how the format adapts to changing tensor magnitudes, enabling longer tested sequences on a memory-constrained GPU without quantizing the stored BF16 values.

**Published:** 2026-10-15 · **First seen:** 2026-10-18T21:44:21.869Z · **Novelty:** material-update · **Tags:** Lossless Compression, Training Memory, GPU Codecs, BF16

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22179>) · [Code](<https://github.com/Maxzhu123/Losslessly_Compressed_Tensors>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Read methodology4.1-4.7, storage/scale analysis5, experiments6 and relevant AppendicesA-C, including timing/memory accounting and training integration. Bounded Huffman prefixes plus literal escapes compress exponents while preserving sign/fraction bytes; dense matrix products still require reconstruction. On one RTX3090 with PyTorch2.14/Triton3.8, activation compression in162M NanoGPT cuts peak allocated memory16058to12103MiB(24.6%) while optimizer-step time rises8.411to9.013s(7.2%). All-component compression yields11964.6MiB/9.136s, and a3400-step run has similar validation loss. Qwen3-4B-Base full-parameter BF16/Muon memory-time tests at batch1 fit3500tested tokens versus1000for the baseline; at1000, memory is21327.8to16262.4MiB with4.006to4.273s step time. This is a new detailed paper/analysis of older public code, not a new implementation release. The prior README says paper-coming-soon; the complete October12 tree contains only a graphical-abstractPDF, not the paper.

**Limitations:** Storage is lossless for input BF16 bit patterns; converting FP32 to BF16 first still loses information, and this does not prove bitwise-identical whole training. Compression depends on exponent statistics, block padding and overflow; small or mismatched tensors can expand. Requires explicit custom-autograd/operator integration, and compressed weights are not ordinary registered nn.Parameters. Shared-arena sizing must include live replacements/fragmentation. Training time/peak memory use only five measured optimizer steps after three warmups; Qwen tests do not establish long-run fine-tuning quality. Reported memory is PyTorch allocated, not allocator-reserved or all device memory; training includes the entire shared arena. Only BF16 is supported here and GEMMs decode first. Code was inspected but not executed; no independent reproduction.

**Update:** 2026-10-16: The newly announced detailed paper adds bounded-code/scale-shift/storage analysis and controlled codec, NanoGPT and Qwen memory-time evaluations to the earlier public LCT implementation (https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22179v1; https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/recent?skip=0&amp;show=2000; https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html). The repository was created October4 with code commits through October12; its README still marks the paper coming soon and its inspected pre-window tree has no paperPDF (https://github.com/Maxzhu123/Losslessly\_Compressed\_Tensors; https://api.github.com/repos/Maxzhu123/Losslessly\_Compressed\_Tensors/git/trees/396b9d6fb725956cb0735a83b5de368319d0b823?recursive=1). ### 3.7 Data Pipelines, Storage &amp; Checkpointing

#### [Coordination-Free Workload Regularization for Variable-Cost Distributed Training](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21162>)

Batch Cost Lookahead buffers a bounded window inside each training worker and regroups it into equal-record-count batches with similar estimated cost, without exchanging sample metadata across workers. This reduces synchronization waiting for variable-length training while retaining the existing batch-count interface, with explicit diagnostics for oversized records and persistent imbalance that local scheduling cannot fix.

Read Sections1-10, Algorithm1 and all evaluation tables. The fixed-cardinality contract conserves each window's records and uses classical longest-processing-time initialization plus bounded heavy/light swaps. On Llama3.2-1B NeMo-RL0.7.0 SFT with FSDP2/BF16/FA3 on eight H200 GPUs, lookahead32 versus1 in the same per-rank pipeline improves mean wall-clock step speed by0.4-30.5% across11 corpora, over three300-step repeats excluding20warmups. All arms use the same per-corpus p99 cap. The abstract's5.0-16.7% comparison against pooledMFFD includes input-path differences and is cross-campaign. Paper receipt is October15 03:22:50Z; public availability is inferred from the original cs.DC Friday16 batch and official Thursday20:00Eastern schedule.

**Limitations:** The assignment heuristic is classical; the contribution is its bounded streaming deployment contract and measured boundary analysis, not a new global optimizer. Length-cost simulation is not GPU speedup. Two matched no-lookahead arms were not rerun after prior OOMs. The larger1.197-1.343x result uses an internal sequential recommender and weak scaling from8to32H200 ranks, not LLM scaling evidence. Local reordering cannot resolve a dominant infeasible record or different total cost across rank shards. It changes optimizer-step sample grouping; p99 truncation quality, held-out SFT quality and exact midstream restart are untested. No dedicated public implementation was verified; no independent reproduction.
